items.title: Frank Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 7, 1998
items.q: that’s why Cecelia Foster does all my business. And whatever success I enjoy, thanks to her.

ctx.x: And managed the day to day operations?

Right. I didn’t have to have anything to do with bookings or the business, and rightly so. Because as a businessman — that’s why Cecelia Foster does all my business. And whatever success I enjoy, thanks to her.
Well that’s a good pairing then.

items.title: Frank Foster and Bill Hughes interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Schenectady, New York, March 28, 1995
items.q: So my wife Cecelia and I got together and we put the lyrics to this song.

ctx.x: What’s this thing about Papa Foss? I heard that song the other day.

That’s what the thing about Papa— it’s a pianist by the name of Danny Mixon who played with me in my small group and he’s a Loud Minority so you know he’s Spacetakovitch, like we all were, and he composed this song called “Papa Foss” [scats]. So he didn’t have any lyrics to it. So my wife Cecelia and I got together and we put the lyrics to this song. and I sold Carmen Bradford on the idea of singing it. And of course it put me out front, you know, “standing out in front of it is Papa Foss, been out in front of it…
Yeah, they’ve been playing it in Syracuse.
